# FreeBSD

FreeBSD platform bindings.

## Installation

Add `FreeBSD` to the `[Dependencies]` table of your package's `Rux.toml`:

```toml
[Dependencies]
FreeBSD = { Namespace = "Rux", Version = "0.1.0" }
```

Standard packages are declared by hand: the registry does not serve them, so `rux add Rux/FreeBSD` cannot add them.

## Dependencies

- [`Core`](/docs/api/core) 0.1.0

## Guide

FreeBSD platform bindings: the raw syscall interface, with no libc in between.

The module names describe where each declaration comes from; they are not part of an import path.

FreeBSD reports an error by setting the carry flag and leaving a _positive_ errno in the result register, so a raw instruction result cannot be tested for sign. The assembly wrappers normalize that to a small negative number, which is Linux's convention, so everything above them reads the same on both systems and [`IsError`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#is-error) and [`Errno`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#errno) are the same two functions.

Nothing here is interchangeable with `Rux/Linux`, and the resemblance is the hazard. The clock identifiers differ — monotonic is 4 here and 1 there — the open flags are the BSD ones, `MADV_DONTNEED` does not discard where Linux's does, and only the errno numbers below thirty-five agree. A value taken from one package and passed to the other compiles and means something else.

[`QueryPageSize`](/docs/api/freebsd/memory#query-page-size) reads the `hw.pagesize` sysctl, which is how FreeBSD publishes the value; there is no dedicated call and no auxiliary vector to read without libc.

### The shared POSIX contract

Nothing here is interchangeable with the other POSIX packages, but the three are _spelled_ the same, which is a different claim and a deliberate one. An equivalent call has the same wrapper name, the same parameter names and the same parameter shapes on all three systems, so a consumer such as [`Rux/FileSystem`](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FreeBSD/../FileSystem) or [`Rux/Time`](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FreeBSD/../Time) writes one call site instead of a `when #target.os` ladder around three names for one idea. `Tests/Unit/PlatformBindingContractTests.cpp` compares the three packages' parsed sources and fails when they drift apart.

The values are the opposite: every constant is this system's own, and the same file asserts that the ones a reader might carry across really do differ.

### What is tested

`Tests/Packages/FreeBSD/Descriptors` covers descriptor numbering, short reads and writes, end of file, size boundaries and the native error for each way of misusing a descriptor or a name. `Tests/Packages/FreeBSD/Mapping` covers anonymous mappings, protection changes, advice, the requests the kernel refuses, and both edges of the reserved error-result window. `Tests/Packages/FreeBSD/Syscall` covers the wrapper surface and the shared POSIX contract.

All of it compiles for both architectures, and none of it has ever run on a host that is not FreeBSD. Until it does, the syscall numbers, flag values and errno constants here rest on published documentation rather than on a passing test.

### Values and pointers

Kernel records such as [`Timespec`](/docs/api/freebsd/timespec) are structural values and copy by value. Syscall wrappers deliberately retain raw pointers because the kernel consumes untyped integer addresses, buffers carry separate lengths, and optional outputs may be null. Pass addresses explicitly, for example `ClockGetTime(ClockMonotonic, @time)`, and uphold each function's safety contract. The package does not own raw addresses or descriptors; release them explicitly or use the higher-level `Rux/Memory` and `Rux/Io` packages.

### Platform

FreeBSD only. Guard use behind a compile-time check, so a build for another target never resolves these declarations:

```rux
import Core::{ #target };

when #target.os {
    .FreeBSD => import FreeBSD::{ StdOut, Write }
}
```

Higher-level packages such as [`Rux/Io`](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FreeBSD/../Io) and [`Rux/Memory`](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FreeBSD/../Memory) already do this, and are the interface to prefer unless you need the syscall itself.

### AArch64 ABI

The AArch64 wrappers follow the FreeBSD syscall convention: the call number is placed in `x8`, up to six wrapper arguments are shifted into `x0` through `x5`, and `svc #0` enters the kernel. A carry-set return is converted from a positive `errno` to the negative result used by the package API.

Descriptor and clock identifiers are sign-extended before entering the generic `uint64` syscall interface. [`Mmap`](/docs/api/freebsd/memory#mmap) likewise preserves a signed descriptor while passing the FreeBSD 15.1 mapping constants and all six arguments directly. The same source keeps a separate set of x86-64 wrappers, which reach the kernel through `syscall` and normalize the carry flag the same way.

| [`ClockMonotonic`](/docs/api/freebsd/clock#clock-monotonic)                     | `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`: time since an unspecified point, which never goes backwards.                                                                                  |

| [`ClockRealtimeFast`](/docs/api/freebsd/clock#clock-realtime-fast)              | `CLOCK_REALTIME_FAST`: like [`ClockRealtime`](/docs/api/freebsd/clock#clock-realtime), read from a cached value.                                                 |
| [`ClockProcessCpuTime`](/docs/api/freebsd/clock#clock-process-cpu-time)         | `CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID`: processor time this process has used.                                                                                                |
| [`RTLD_LAZY`](/docs/api/freebsd/dynamic#rtld-lazy)                              | `RTLD_LAZY`: resolve a function symbol the first time it is called rather than at load.                                                                          |
| [`RTLD_NOW`](/docs/api/freebsd/dynamic#rtld-now)                                | `RTLD_NOW`: resolve every symbol before [`dlopen`](/docs/api/freebsd/dynamic#dlopen) returns.                                                                    |
| [`RTLD_GLOBAL`](/docs/api/freebsd/dynamic#rtld-global)                          | `RTLD_GLOBAL`: make this object's symbols available to objects loaded afterwards.                                                                                |
| [`RTLD_LOCAL`](/docs/api/freebsd/dynamic#rtld-local)                            | `RTLD_LOCAL`: keep this object's symbols to itself, which is the default.                                                                                        |
| [`RandomNonBlocking`](/docs/api/freebsd/get-random#random-non-blocking)         | `GRND_NONBLOCK`: report rather than wait.                                                                                                                        |
| [`RandomBlockingPool`](/docs/api/freebsd/get-random#random-blocking-pool)       | `GRND_RANDOM`: accepted and ignored, which is what FreeBSD does with it.                                                                                         |
| [`EPERM`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#eperm)                                       | `EPERM`: the operation is not permitted to this caller.                                                                                                          |
| [`ENOENT`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#enoent)                                     | `ENOENT`: no such file or directory.                                                                                                                             |
| [`ESRCH`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#esrch)                                       | `ESRCH`: no such process.                                                                                                                                        |
| [`EINTR`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#eintr)                                       | `EINTR`: the call was interrupted by a signal before it did anything.                                                                                            |
| [`EIO`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#eio)                                           | `EIO`: a low-level input or output error.                                                                                                                        |
| [`ENXIO`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#enxio)                                       | `ENXIO`: no such device or address.                                                                                                                              |

| [`ENOMEM`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#enomem)                                     | `ENOMEM`: not enough memory to satisfy the request.                                                                                                              |
| [`EACCES`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#eacces)                                     | `EACCES`: permission denied.                                                                                                                                     |
| [`EFAULT`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#efault)                                     | `EFAULT`: an address the call was given is outside the caller's address space.                                                                                   |
| [`EBUSY`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#ebusy)                                       | `EBUSY`: the resource is in use.                                                                                                                                 |
| [`EEXIST`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#eexist)                                     | `EEXIST`: the file already exists.                                                                                                                               |
| [`EXDEV`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#exdev)                                       | `EXDEV`: the two paths are on different file systems.                                                                                                            |
| [`ENOTDIR`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#enotdir)                                   | `ENOTDIR`: a path component that had to be a directory is not one.                                                                                               |
| [`EISDIR`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#eisdir)                                     | `EISDIR`: the target is a directory and the operation is not one a directory accepts.                                                                            |
| [`EINVAL`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#einval)                                     | `EINVAL`: an argument is not valid.                                                                                                                              |
| [`EMFILE`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#emfile)                                     | `EMFILE`: this process has too many descriptors open.                                                                                                            |
| [`ENOSPC`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#enospc)                                     | `ENOSPC`: the device has no room left.                                                                                                                           |
| [`ESPIPE`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#espipe)                                     | `ESPIPE`: the descriptor is a pipe or socket and cannot be seeked.                                                                                               |

| [`EPIPE`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#epipe)                                       | `EPIPE`: the reading end of the pipe is closed.                                                                                                                  |
| [`ENAMETOOLONG`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#enametoolong)                         | `ENAMETOOLONG`: the path or a component of it is too long.                                                                                                       |
| [`ELOOP`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#eloop)                                       | `ELOOP`: too many symbolic links were followed resolving the path.                                                                                               |
| [`ENOSYS`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#enosys)                                     | `ENOSYS`: the kernel does not implement this call.                                                                                                               |
| [`EOVERFLOW`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#eoverflow)                               | `EOVERFLOW`: a value is too large for the type the call reports it in.                                                                                           |
| [`ETIMEDOUT`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#etimedout)                               | `ETIMEDOUT`: the operation timed out.                                                                                                                            |
| [`MaximumErrno`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#maximum-errno)                        | The largest error number the normalized error range holds.                                                                                                       |
| [`StdIn`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#std-in)                                       | The descriptor a process reads its input from, unless something reassigned it.                                                                                   |
| [`StdOut`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#std-out)                                     | The descriptor a process writes its output to.                                                                                                                   |
| [`StdErr`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#std-err)                                     | The descriptor a process writes its diagnostics to.                                                                                                              |
| [`AtFdCwd`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#at-fd-cwd)                                  | `AT_FDCWD`: resolve a relative path against the current directory rather than a descriptor.                                                                      |
| [`OpenReadOnly`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#open-read-only)                        | `O_RDONLY`: open for reading only.                                                                                                                               |

| [`OpenReadWrite`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#open-read-write)                      | `O_RDWR`: open for both reading and writing.                                                                                                                     |
| [`OpenCreate`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#open-create)                             | `O_CREAT`: create the file when it does not exist, which is when the mode argument is read.                                                                      |

| [`OpenAppend`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#open-append)                             | `O_APPEND`: every write goes to the end.                                                                                                                         |
| [`OpenNonBlocking`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#open-non-blocking)                  | [`O_NONBLOCK`](/docs/api/freebsd/poll#o-nonblock): reads and writes report [`EAGAIN`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#eagain) rather than waiting.                      |
| [`OpenCloseOnExec`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#open-close-on-exec)                 | `O_CLOEXEC`: close this descriptor automatically when the process executes a new program.                                                                        |
| [`OpenDirectory`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#open-directory)                       | `O_DIRECTORY`: fail unless the target is a directory.                                                                                                            |

| [`SeekCurrent`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#seek-current)                           | `SEEK_CUR`: measure the new offset from the current one.                                                                                                         |
| [`SeekEnd`](/docs/api/freebsd/files#seek-end)                                   | `SEEK_END`: measure the new offset from the end of the file.                                                                                                     |
| [`RemoveDirectory`](/docs/api/freebsd/directories#remove-directory)             | `AT_REMOVEDIR`: make [`UnlinkAt`](/docs/api/freebsd/directories#unlink-at) remove a directory rather than a file.                                                |
| [`SymlinkNoFollow`](/docs/api/freebsd/directories#symlink-no-follow)            | `AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW`: act on a symbolic link itself rather than on what it points at.                                                                           |
| [`FollowSymlinks`](/docs/api/freebsd/directories#follow-symlinks)               | `AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW`: make [`LinkAt`](/docs/api/freebsd/directories#link-at) link a symbolic link's target rather than the link.                                  |
| [`ProtectionNone`](/docs/api/freebsd/memory#protection-none)                    | `PROT_NONE`: the pages may not be touched at all.                                                                                                                |
| [`ProtectionRead`](/docs/api/freebsd/memory#protection-read)                    | `PROT_READ`: the pages may be read.                                                                                                                              |
| [`ProtectionWrite`](/docs/api/freebsd/memory#protection-write)                  | `PROT_WRITE`: the pages may be written.                                                                                                                          |
| [`ProtectionExecute`](/docs/api/freebsd/memory#protection-execute)              | `PROT_EXEC`: the pages may be executed.                                                                                                                          |

| [`MapPrivate`](/docs/api/freebsd/memory#map-private)                            | `MAP_PRIVATE`: writes are private to this mapping and never reach the object.                                                                                    |

| [`AdviseDontNeed`](/docs/api/freebsd/memory#advise-dont-need)                   | `MADV_DONTNEED`: the pages are not needed soon.                                                                                                                  |

| [`CtlHardware`](/docs/api/freebsd/memory#ctl-hw)                                | `CTL_HW`: the sysctl branch describing the machine.                                                                                                              |
| [`HardwarePageSize`](/docs/api/freebsd/memory#hw-pagesize)                      | `HW_PAGESIZE`: the leaf under [`CtlHardware`](/docs/api/freebsd/memory#ctl-hw) holding the page size, in bytes.                                                  |
| [`F_GETFL`](/docs/api/freebsd/poll#f-getfl)                                     | [`F_SETFD`](/docs/api/freebsd/spawn#f-setfd)'s companion `F_GETFL`: the [`fcntl`](/docs/api/freebsd/spawn#fcntl) command that reads a descriptor's status flags. |
| [`F_SETFL`](/docs/api/freebsd/poll#f-setfl)                                     | `F_SETFL`: the [`fcntl`](/docs/api/freebsd/spawn#fcntl) command that sets a descriptor's status flags.                                                           |
| [`O_NONBLOCK`](/docs/api/freebsd/poll#o-nonblock)                               | `O_NONBLOCK`: the status flag that makes a call fail with [`EAGAIN`](/docs/api/freebsd/errors#eagain) rather than wait.                                          |

| [`EV_DELETE`](/docs/api/freebsd/poll#ev-delete)                                 | `EV_DELETE`: remove the change's filter.                                                                                                                         |
